Short answers to "how do I ...?". The recipes share the objects built in
[Tutorial: Your First Coverage Study](tutorial-first-study.html). Run this setup
first: it defines the `sobel` method, the `truth` function, the tutorial's two
`scenarios`, a `config` and a finished `results` object.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(medsim)

sobel <- function(data, params) {
  fm <- summary(lm(M ~ X, data = data))$coefficients
  fy <- summary(lm(Y ~ X + M, data = data))$coefficients
  a  <- fm["X", "Estimate"]; sa <- fm["X", "Std. Error"]
  b  <- fy["M", "Estimate"]; sb <- fy["M", "Std. Error"]
  se <- sqrt(b^2 * sa^2 + a^2 * sb^2)
  list(indirect = a * b, indirect_se = se,
       indirect_ci_lower = a * b - 1.96 * se,
       indirect_ci_upper = a * b + 1.96 * se,
       indirect_p = 2 * pnorm(-abs(a * b / se)))
}
truth <- function(data, params) list(indirect = params$indirect)

two_path <- function(a, b, name) {
  medsim_scenario(
    name = name,
    data_generator = function(n) {
      X <- rnorm(n); M <- a * X + rnorm(n); Y <- b * M + rnorm(n)
      data.frame(X = X, M = M, Y = Y)
    },
    params = list(a = a, b = b, indirect = a * b)
  )
}
scenarios <- list(two_path(0.39, 0.39, "Medium"), two_path(0, 0.39, "Null (a = 0)"))
config    <- medsim_config("local", n_replications = 500, output_dir = tempdir())
results   <- medsim_run(sobel, scenarios, config, compute_truth = truth)
```

## Design

### Build a factorial grid of scenarios

Generate scenarios from a parameter grid rather than writing them by hand. Put
every design factor in the name: names seed the replications, and they become
the row labels of every table.

```{r}
#| label: grid
grid <- expand.grid(a = c(0, 0.14, 0.39), b = c(0, 0.39))

make_scenario <- function(a, b) {
  medsim_scenario(
    name = sprintf("a=%.2f b=%.2f", a, b),
    data_generator = function(n) {
      X <- rnorm(n)
      M <- a * X + rnorm(n)
      Y <- b * M + rnorm(n)
      data.frame(X = X, M = M, Y = Y)
    },
    params = list(a = a, b = b, indirect = a * b)
  )
}
grid_scenarios <- Map(make_scenario, grid$a, grid$b)
length(grid_scenarios)
#> [1] 6
```

### Vary the sample size

`medsim_run()` calls every generator with `n = config$n` (200 by default). To
study several sample sizes, run once per size and stack the analyses:

```{r}
#| label: sample-size
config <- medsim_config("local", n_replications = 500)
sizes <- c(100, 200, 500)
by_n <- lapply(sizes, function(n) {
  config$n <- n
  medsim_run(sobel, grid_scenarios, config, compute_truth = truth)
})

# Scenario names repeat across the runs, so tag each analysis with its n
power_by_n <- do.call(rbind, Map(function(res, n) {
  cbind(n = n, medsim_analyze_power(res)$by_scenario)
}, by_n, sizes))
power_by_n[power_by_n$scenario == "a=0.14 b=0.39", c("n", "scenario", "power")]
#>      n      scenario power
#> 5  100 a=0.14 b=0.39 0.176
#> 11 200 a=0.14 b=0.39 0.460
#> 17 500 a=0.14 b=0.39 0.858
```

Each run in `by_n` analyzes on its own. Because the scenario names repeat, keep
the `n` column when you stack results; without it the sample sizes would be
indistinguishable.

Set `config$n` after `medsim_config()` returns. Passing `n = 100` to
`medsim_config()` fails, because `n` partially matches `n_replications`,
`n_cores` and `n_chunks`.

If the sample size must vary *within* one run (for example, on a cluster array),
make it a scenario parameter and have the generator ignore the runner's `n`:

```{r}
#| label: n-in-scenario
make_scenario_n <- function(a, b, size) {
  medsim_scenario(
    name = sprintf("a=%.2f b=%.2f n=%d", a, b, size),
    data_generator = function(n) {   # runner's n deliberately ignored
      X <- rnorm(size)
      M <- a * X + rnorm(size)
      Y <- b * M + rnorm(size)
      data.frame(X = X, M = M, Y = Y)
    },
    params = list(a = a, b = b, n = size, indirect = a * b)
  )
}
```

::: {.callout-warning}
`medsim_run()` computes the truth from one large draw, `data_generator(n = 10000)`.
A generator that ignores `n` hands `compute_truth` a sample of size `size`
instead. That is harmless when the truth comes from `params`, as here, but
wrong when `compute_truth` estimates the truth from the data.
:::

### Nonnormal variables

`medsim_rnonnormal()` draws from a distribution with a given mean, SD,
skewness and excess kurtosis (Fleishman's power method). Use it for a
predictor, a mediator residual or an outcome residual:

```{r}
#| label: nonnormal
nonnormal_generator <- function(n) {
  X <- rnorm(n)
  M <- 0.39 * X + medsim_rnonnormal(n, skew = 2, kurtosis = 7)
  Y <- 0.39 * M + rnorm(n)
  data.frame(X = X, M = M, Y = Y)
}
```

Check a new skew-kurtosis pair before you rely on it: in a draw of 200,000 the
sample skewness and excess kurtosis should be close to the targets. The pair
above gives about 1.97 and 6.5.

### Missing data

`medsim_amputate()` removes values from one variable under MCAR, MAR or MNAR.
Apply it inside the generator, after the complete data are drawn:

```{r}
#| label: amputate
missing_generator <- function(n) {
  X <- rnorm(n)
  M <- 0.39 * X + rnorm(n)
  Y <- 0.39 * M + rnorm(n)
  medsim_amputate(data.frame(X = X, M = M, Y = Y),
                  target = "M", mechanism = "MAR", prop = 0.3,
                  predictors = "X")
}
set.seed(1)
colMeans(is.na(missing_generator(200)))
#>     X     M     Y
#> 0.000 0.335 0.000
```

`prop` is a target proportion, so each data set's realized rate varies around
it. For full missing-data designs (grids over mechanism, rate and
nonnormality, and the MI estimators), see the
[Missing-Data Mediation](missing-data-mediation.html) article.

## Running

### Smoke-test before a long run

```{r}
#| label: smoke
smoke <- medsim_run(sobel, scenarios, medsim_config("test"),
                    compute_truth = truth)
stopifnot(all(is.na(smoke$results$error)))
```

Twenty replications per scenario take seconds and catch a broken method or
generator before you spend hours on it.

### Choose the number of replications

```{r}
#| label: nsim
medsim_nsim_for_mcse(target_mcse = 0.005, p = 0.95)  # coverage near .95
#> [1] 1900
medsim_nsim_for_mcse(target_mcse = 0.005, p = 0.05)  # type I error near .05
#> [1] 1900
medsim_nsim_for_mcse(target_mcse = 0.01,  p = 0.5)   # worst case (power near .5)
#> [1] 2500
```

### Keep a scratch run out of your project

`medsim_run()` caches truth values in the configuration's `output_dir`. Point it
at a temporary directory for throwaway runs:

```{r}
#| label: tempdir
config <- medsim_config("test", output_dir = tempdir())
```

### Use several cores

`medsim_run(..., parallel = TRUE)` (the default) spreads replications over
`config$n_cores` workers. Set the count explicitly, or let `medsim` pick it:

```{r}
#| label: cores
config <- medsim_config("local", n_cores = 4)
medsim_detect_cores()                         # cores on this machine
medsim_get_optimal_cores(n_tasks = 1000)      # leaves 2 cores free by default
```

Results do not depend on the number of cores: each replication is seeded from
its scenario name and replication number, not from the worker it runs on.

### Methods that sometimes fail

You don't need to wrap a method in `tryCatch()`. `medsim_run()` catches the
error, records its message in the `error` column, and moves on:

```{r}
#| label: failures
flaky <- function(data, params) {
  if (runif(1) < 0.2) stop("did not converge")
  sobel(data, params)
}
res <- medsim_run(flaky, scenarios, config, compute_truth = truth)
table(res$results$error, useNA = "ifany")
```

`medsim_analyze_coverage()` reports the failures per scenario (`n_failed`,
`failure_rate`) and computes coverage over the replications that succeeded.
Report the failure rate next to coverage: a method that fails on the hardest
data sets looks better than it is.

### Run on a SLURM cluster

Split the replications into chunks, run one chunk per array task, then combine
under an integrity audit. You can dry-run the whole array on your own machine
by looping over the chunk IDs that SLURM would assign:

```{r}
#| label: cluster
cl_config <- medsim_config("cluster", n_replications = 200, n_chunks = 4,
                           output_dir = file.path(tempdir(), "sim_out"))
medsim_write_submit_script(cl_config)   # writes submit_array.sh

# On the cluster each array task runs one chunk (chunk_id comes from
# SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID). Locally, loop over the IDs:
for (id in seq_len(cl_config$n_chunks)) {
  cl_config$chunk_id <- id
  medsim_run_chunk(scenarios, sobel, cl_config, compute_truth = truth)
}

combined <- medsim_combine_chunks(cl_config$output_dir,
                                  expected_chunks = cl_config$n_chunks)
table(combined$results$scenario)
#>
#>       Medium Null (a = 0)
#>          200          200
```

`medsim_combine_chunks()` returns an ordinary `medsim_results` object. Pass
`compute_truth` to every chunk: without it the combined object carries no truth,
and `medsim_analyze_coverage()` and `medsim_analyze()` have nothing to score
against. Only chunk 1 computes it; the other chunks ignore the argument but
record that truth was requested, so if chunk 1's truth is lost the combine
raises a `truth_coverage` violation instead of quietly returning no truth:

```{r}
#| label: cluster-coverage
medsim_analyze_coverage(combined, ci_levels = 0.95)$by_scenario[
  , c("scenario", "coverage", "n_valid")]
#>       scenario coverage n_valid
#> 1       Medium     0.94     200
#> 2 Null (a = 0)     0.95     200
```

Chunk 1 runs longer than the others, since it also computes truth. For a
production array, compute truth once before you submit, by running
`medsim_run()` over the same scenarios and `output_dir`. Every chunk then
finds the truth in the cache. (Set `config$compute_truth_every_chunk <- TRUE`
only if truth is cheap and chunk 1 may not finish.)

The [Cluster Testing](cluster-testing.html) article covers the two-tier testing
model, chunk sizing and the audit checks.

## Saving and reporting

### Save and reload results

```{r}
#| label: cache
medsim_cache_save(results, "results/sobel.rds")
results <- medsim_cache_load("results/sobel.rds")
```

`medsim_cache_save()` compresses by default. `medsim_cache_list("results")`
lists the cached files in a directory, `medsim_cache_info()` describes one
file, and `medsim_cache_clear("results")` removes them (it asks first).

### Bias with Monte Carlo SEs

`medsim_analyze_performance()` reads `<param>_truth` from the results table,
which `medsim_run()` stores separately. Merge it in first:

```{r}
#| label: performance
tr <- results$truth
names(tr)[-1] <- paste0(names(tr)[-1], "_truth")
medsim_analyze_performance(merge(results$results, tr, by = "scenario"))
```

### Write a table as CSV or Markdown

`medsim_write_table()` picks the format from the file extension (`.tex`,
`.csv`, `.md`) and creates the directory if needed:

```{r}
#| label: write-table
cov <- medsim_analyze_coverage(results, ci_levels = 0.95)
medsim_write_table(medsim_table_coverage(cov), "tables/coverage.csv")
```

CSV output drops the LaTeX formatting (it warns you), so keep the `.tex`
version for the manuscript.

### Restyle a figure

Plots are `ggplot2` objects:

```{r}
#| label: restyle
library(ggplot2)
medsim_plot_coverage(cov) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  labs(title = NULL)
```
